Alright, let me think through this year's plan. I'll reason as the farmer, then put it down in the structured format.

---

My name isn't important — what matters is I've been working these 9.5 mu for 35 years now, since I was 23. My husband helps, and our son when he's back from the city. I went through middle school, so I can read the bags on the fertilizer and understand when the extension fellow comes around, but most of what I know comes from doing it year after year and watching what works on my neighbors' fields.

Let me think about each crop.

**Cotton** — this is my main crop, it's what our village does. I'll put about 4 mu in cotton. Plant mid-to-late April, once the soil warms up. I use the improved seed from the agricultural supply shop in town — the one my neighbor Li's wife has been buying, she says it yields better than the old kind. Last year I got about 260 kg lint per mu, which was okay. I put down compound fertilizer before planting, maybe 40 kg of 15-15-15 per mu, and then topdress with urea at squaring, about 15 kg per mu. That comes to roughly 16 kg of N per mu total — the extension person said I could do more but I've been doing this and it's fine. I'll spray for bollworm when I see them, and maybe two or three sprays against aphids. Irrigation — I'll water once before planting if it's been dry, and maybe once more at flowering. Cotton doesn't like too much water. The picking is the hard part, me and my husband handle most of it but I hire two women from the village for a few days at peak.

**Cauliflower** — I'll put 3 mu in cauliflower, spring planting, transplant out in early April, harvest end of May and into June before it gets too hot. Cauliflower pays well at the market if the timing is right, but it's a lot of work and needs water. I buy seedlings from the nursery, about 80 yuan per mu worth. This crop is hungry — needs more fertilizer than cotton. I'll put down chicken manure if I can get it, plus about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before transplanting, then topdress twice with urea. That's maybe 20 kg N per mu total. I irrigate 5 or 6 times through the season — cauliflower heads won't form right if it dries out. After the cauliflower comes out in June, the land mostly rests or I'll put in some late vegetables for the family.

**Stevia** — I have 2.5 mu on contract with the company that comes through. They provide the seedlings and tell us what to do, sort of. I transplant in mid-April, harvest the leaves in August, sometimes a second cut in September if it's been a good year. I use less fertilizer on stevia than cauliflower, maybe 12 kg N per mu and some compound. Irrigate 3 times or so. The company buys the dried leaves at a set price — not great, but it's steady money and we have the contract.

Money-wise, I have to watch it. I'll spend maybe 4,500-5,000 yuan on inputs total this season. I always keep some cash back for emergencies — last time we had an early frost on the cauliflower I had to replant part of it, that cost us. You can't plan for everything but you can leave yourself a little room.

Yields — I'm hoping for similar to last year. Cotton 260 kg lint, cauliflower around 2,000 kg per mu of heads, stevia 150 kg of dried leaves per mu. If the weather cooperates.
